1.explanation:
• printDocToString (in doc-printer.js) is responsible for converting the internal Doc representation into a final string and appending the final newline. If it unconditionally adds a hardline or fails to account for existing trailing newlines, it can introduce an extra blank line.
• trim (in doc-printer.js) performs whitespace trimming at the end of lines. Its logic may not remove an extra hardline at the very end of the file, causing two newlines to remain.
• printPathNoParens (in printer-estree.js) handles printing of the Program node, including directives like 'use strict'. It contains the logic “Only force a trailing newline if there were any contents,” and may incorrectly decide to add a second newline when printing a directive followed by a comment. Adjusting its trailing-newline condition or how it marks content will prevent the duplicate blank line.
1.bug_scenario: When a file contains nothing but a directive (e.g. 'use strict') followed by a blank line and then a comment, Prettier emits two trailing newlines instead of one. In the provided screenshot you can see the input with a directive and a comment, and on the right side Prettier’s output ends with an extra blank line.

2.explanation: The extra newline originates in the document printer’s whitespace‐trimming and final stringification logic. The trim() function in src/document/doc-printer.js is responsible for dropping trailing spaces and line endings, but currently it leaves one too many hardlines when a comment immediately follows a directive. The printDocToString() function invokes trim() on the accumulated output and then always appends a terminating newline, so any extra hardline left by trim() turns into two newlines. Meanwhile, in src/language-js/printer-estree.js the printPathNoParens() function that handles the Program’s InterpreterDirective also unconditionally forces a trailing newline when there is content, even in the special case of a lone directive plus comment. Fixing either or both—by having trim() collapse multiple trailing hardlines into one, and/or by making printPathNoParens() only add a single newline when no code follows the comment—will correct the behavior so that the final output ends with exactly one newline.
2.bug_scenario: When formatting a JS file that consists of only a "use strict" directive followed by a comment, Prettier currently emits two trailing newlines instead of a single one. The playground screenshot shows the input of a directive and a comment, and the formatted output ends in an extra blank line.
